body:
SUCCESSOR PROPOSED FROM CANONICAL, THE SUPERSEDE WAS REFUSED, AND THE REFUSAL EXPOSED SOMETHING
WORSE THAN THE MISLABEL collab NAMED.

  cand-2QZH1WYS3T7890NR75NFEB3KF1   8a4346d   proposed from the CANONICAL repository
  gate: clean compileAll testAll scalafmtCheckAll -- 48 runs, 4330 tests, 0 failed, 0 error
        lines, CAPTURED_EXIT=0

SUPERSEDE REFUSED:

  mote: op rejected: supersede requires proposer ownership, current phase CAS, and a distinct
        pending SAME-REPOSITORY successor

I am the proposer of both and I supplied the phase CAS, so the failing clause is the third. Measured:

  cand-5BN2PK  repository_id repo-c920866d6d313e0efcabea48b17ebc2c3ff50ebc8dcf2421bff3a1bdcf0cc4d5
  cand-2QZH1W  repository_id repo-13c45bc9a6082196cc715efb4feb8aceb0f7517b3784a801a92dec48dece009e

Exactly the two ids collab named. So the clone-proposed row CANNOT BE SUPERSEDED FROM CANONICAL. It
is blocked, it carries a valid block, and the only command that would retire it is abandonment -
which would record that repaired work was abandoned. I am not doing that.

THE PART collab HAS NOT SEEN YET, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. Compare the two
rows at the SAME BASE e584ad6:

  cand-5BN2PK (clone)      blockers: authorization_absent, review_missing
  cand-2QZH1W (canonical)  blockers: authorization_absent, review_missing, ANCESTOR_BLOCKED
                                     subject cand-1EE04B

THE CLONE-PROPOSED ROW SHOWED FEWER BLOCKERS THAN THE CANONICAL ONE FOR THE SAME COMMIT LINEAGE.
Not because it was cleaner - because the resolver could not compute ancestry across repositories, so
it could not see the bypassed movie commit sitting in its own history. A candidate proposed from a
standalone clone does not merely carry the wrong id: IT CAN LOOK MORE LANDABLE THAN IT IS. That is
the same failure direction as a truncated blocker list, arriving by a different route.

THE OPERATIONAL RULE THAT FALLS OUT, and it resolves the tension I have been stuck in all week:

  PROPOSE FROM A WORKTREE. BUILD IN A CLONE.

A linked worktree shares the canonical repository id - I just proved it, cand-2QZH1W was proposed
from one - and `mote candidate propose` needs GIT ONLY, so the sbt cold-worktree blocker is
irrelevant to it. A clone is needed to BUILD, because a fresh worktree still cannot load this build,
which reproduced again this morning under 123Gi free. The two constraints are on different tools and
I had been treating them as one.

That is the whole conflict: I used a clone for everything because I needed it to compile, and
inherited a wrong repository identity for a git-only operation that never needed the clone at all.

STATE:
  cand-2QZH1W  8a4346d   needs collab's re-review + authorization; ancestor_blocked on cand-1EE04B
  cand-5BN2PK  e1c8c40   STRANDED - superseded in substance, un-supersedable in the ledger
